target: connate (FLOPO_0991067), restricted to the base of the filament
fix: In 'connate/fused for X mm' the number is how far the fusion runs. It is not the length of the organ. Read it as connate, and keep the number on the fused zone (or drop it), never as the organ's length.
reason: The 1-2 mm is how far the outer filaments are joined at the base. The stamens themselves are 1.2-1.7 cm long. So 'filament length 1-2 mm' is false.

The calyx lobes are sepals, and '± orbicular' becomes orbicular with 'approximately'. The text is about male flowers only, but the female calyx lobes have no conflicting shape, so the statement still holds.

fix: 'Sub-' + an inflorescence type (subspicate, subumbellate, subpaniculate) describes the form of the inflorescence. It does not say a true spike is present. Annotate the inflorescence with a spike-like form, or reject it if there is no term.
reason: The inflorescence only looks somewhat like a spike: its capitula sit along a branch. Saying 'a spike inflorescence is present' claims something the flora does not say.
The flora says the branch leaves are 'not undulate'. Undulate is negated on the leaf (phyllid), and the negation covers only that word.
'Dépourvue de caoutchouc' means the plant has no rubber or latex. 'Latex present', negated, says that.
The flora says 'stamens 5', so the stamen count is 5.

fix: In a list such as 'corolla ..., limb lobes lanceolate, apically acuminate', the later qualities belong to the last part named (the lobes), not to the head word (the corolla).
reason: It is the corolla limb lobes that are acuminate at the apex, not the whole corolla.

fix: Map 'papyracé', papery and chartaceous to PATO_0104010. Do not use bare 'texture' with no value.
reason: 'Papyracé' means papery. Bare 'texture' loses the meaning, and a PATO term exists.

fix: 'Margins X' after a part means the margin of that part: use the margin class, or the bract with a margin restriction. Also, 'sub-' before the value should add the 'approximately' qualifier.
reason: Only the margins of the phyllaries are submembranous, not the whole bract. The bracts are green to purplish.
The flora says 4-6 secondary veins on each side of the midvein. The annotation has that count and the 'each side' position.
The flora says 'at maturity 80-120 ft tall'. That is 24.4-36.6 m, and the mature context is recorded.

target: stem dichotomously branched, 2-4 times (number of branchings)
fix: 'N times branched/forked' counts how many times the stem forks in a row. It does not count branches; 2 forkings give up to 4 tips. Do not map it to the amount of branches.
reason: '2-4 times dichotomously branched' means the stem forks 2-4 times. It does not mean the stem has 2-4 branches.
A single seed size in FNA is its length, so seed length is 1.2-1.5 mm.
In older floras, 'strict' means erect and straight, so 'flower erect' fits.
The flora says racemes are up to 25 cm long in fruit. The annotation has that limit and the fruiting-stage context.

target: the part compared to: inflorescence (PO_0009049), not capitulum inflorescence (PO_0030121)
fix: 'Head' in Carex and other sedges, rushes and grasses means a compact cluster of spikes. It is a capitulum only in daisies (Asteraceae) and similar families. Ground 'head' by family.
reason: The bract is shorter than the Carex head, which is a cluster of spikes, not a capitulum. The word was grounded to the wrong part.
'3(-7)-foliolate' means usually 3 leaflets and up to 7. The annotation has a count of 3 per leaf with a maximum of 7.
The flora says the floral bract is membranaceous, so 'bract membranous' fits.
The flora says the leaf blade is dark green when mature, and the mature context is recorded.

fix: When a flora names a position-qualified member (posterior, lateral, outer, inner), keep the position. Without it, the statement contradicts the other members. Also, 'or rarely Y' should put 'rarely' on Y only.
reason: Only the posterior sepal is orange; the flora says the lateral sepals are green or purplish. Also, 'rarely' is set on the whole annotation, but it belongs to pink only.
In French floras, 'médiocre' means of middling size, so 'flower medium-sized' fits.
The flora says 5-7 florets per spikelet. The annotation counts flowers inside the spikelet.
The flora says the corolla is 5-lobed, so it has 5 corolla lobes.
The flora says the drupe is 'ellipsoid or oblong'. Ellipsoid maps to prolate and oblong maps to oblong.
The flora says the stipes have dense hairs distally. The annotation has the stalk as hairy on its distal part.
The flora says the petal apex is rounded. 'Rounded' maps to obtuse, whose synonym is 'roundish', and the bearer is the petal apex.

target: flower (PO_0009046) in the inflorescence, amount several to many
fix: 'X-flowered' / 'several to many flowered' counts flowers in the inflorescence. The flower is the bearer, with the inflorescence as its whole. Also keep the whole range ('several to many'), not only 'several'.
reason: The statement gives how many flowers each cyme has. It does not say 'an inflorescence is present'.
The flora says both blade surfaces are tomentose when young. The annotation has the blade as tomentose with the young context.
'1-seeded' means 1 seed per fruit. The 'per fruit' whole is not recorded but would add precision.
'Graines nombreuses' means seeds many: seeds present, with the count word 'many'.
